title: Palm Harbor Invitational
logline: Michael stages a Scranton-Stamford Office Outing at a mini golf course, where Pam hides from Jim behind a windmill until she finally talks to him, and Michael learns that being present beats being the favorite.
outline: A: Michael's Office Outing at Palm Harbor Mini Golf and Grille, Scranton and Stamford together; Angela's Party Planning pavilion clashes with his plan; Pam avoids Jim, then talks to him (Michael drives the outing). B: Michael tries to win the office with trophies, skips Toby, then asks Toby how he is; Dwight and Andy's grudging partnership for the Monday call. C: Stanley 188 to 187 with Creed in the parking lot. Order: cold, A, B, A, C, A, B, A, B, A, tag.
theme: Being present: choosing who you are with over who you could be.
storySoFar: Jim is in Stamford dating Shannon Doyle and working with Karen Filippelli, who joined his hologram prank. Pam's unanswered card and unsent drafts sit in her reception drawer; she has a secret Tuesday watercolor class. Michael took the blame for the hologram to protect Pam and Jim, and says he won't lie for her again. Michael's Jan lunch failed; Jan calls his kindness disgusting. The office intervened and Toby told Michael to be present. Dwight and Andy are grudging partners for Monday's 3 p.m. Corporate call with David Wallace. Roy has set a June 14 wedding date. Stanley is at 188 days; Kevin closes every countdown joke with "Nobody say nothing." Today: the Scranton-Stamford Office Outing at Palm Harbor Mini Golf and Grille.

stateChanges.status: dating, brought to the Scranton outing
a first real question asked; Michael tries to be present with him
talking again in person; Pam says she read the card three times and has something to tell him, not here

stateChanges.text: Pam says she has something to tell Jim; the Tuesday class and Michael covering on the phone are still unrevealed.
Roy at the outing with his June 14 binder; he is suspicious of Jim and told Halpert not to make Pam sad.
Michael's Mini Golf Invitational trophy is a bowling pin spray-painted gold, a callback to the earlier Invitational pin.
Monday 3 p.m. Corporate call with David Wallace: Dwight and Andy plan to share the presentation.
Michael's 'That's what she said' dies on silence to Stanley's countdown (188 cold open, 187 tag); Kevin closes with 'Nobody say nothing.'
Andy's bear-paw phone plays banjo hold music; Oscar: 'Actually, that's a banjo on hold.'
Michael keeps 'accidentally' calling kindness the disgusting thing Jan called it; Kelly says it too at the toast.

stateChanges.progress: Jim visits for the outing; Pam avoids him, then talks to him at the windmill. She has read the card three times and says they need to talk, not here. The card is still unanswered.

stateChanges.arc: Michael Wants to Be the Favorite
stateChanges.progress: Michael's trophies fail; he sits with Toby and asks how he is, and it lands. He is learning to be present.

stateChanges.arc: Dwight vs Andy for Number Two
stateChanges.progress: Dwight and Andy are working as grudging partners for the Monday call, sharing the presentation.

scenes.recap: Michael tries the countdown joke on Stanley at 188 days, and it dies on silence until Kevin closes it.

beats.caption: eats a fistful of M&Ms from a paper cup

beats.text: Stanley, 188 days. You're almost there. That's what she said.

beats.caption: Stanley does not look up from his crossword.

beats.text: Seven across. Four letters. Final answer: leave.
Nobody say nothing.

scenes.recap: Michael announces the Office Outing at Palm Harbor, and Angela says the Party Planning Committee already booked the pavilion.

beats.text: Scranton and Stamford, one day, one family. Palm Harbor Mini Golf and Grille, Saturday.
The Party Planning Committee has reserved the pavilion for a Garden Party.
A garden party is for people who are scared of windmills.
Actually, mini golf is a sport, not a party. The pavilion is still a pavilion.

lines: I want everyone to have fun. Mostly I want everyone to have fun because of me.
Is that bad? Don't answer that. Toby, don't answer that.

beats.text: Angela, you get the pavilion. I get the holes. Everybody wins.
Pam, Jim's coming, and Karen, and Shannon. Shannon is his girlfriend.
Great. Mini golf.

scenes.recap: Dwight and Andy argue over who drives the van and who talks on Monday's call, while Andy's banjo hold music rings out.

beats.text: Question: who is driving the van to Palm Harbor? Me, because I have seniority over your sweater.
Partners share the van, Dwight. Deep breath. Partners.

beats.caption: bear-paw phone plays banjo hold music across the bullpen

beats.text: Actually, that's a banjo on hold.

lines: Dwight and I are partners for the Monday three o'clock call with David Wallace.
I'm working on my anger. Mostly the anger about the van. Also the anger about Dwight's scarf.

beats.text: False. You have no scarf. You have a banjo, which is worse.
Fine. You drive. I talk. Big Tuna's going to hear about this.

scenes.recap: Kelly learns Jim is bringing a girlfriend, and she finds Pam's drawer of folded drafts.

beats.text: Jim is bringing a girlfriend! Shannon! Do you know how that feels?
Shannon sounds nice.

beats.caption: peeks into Pam's reception drawer full of folded drafts

beats.text: That is personal, Kelly.

lines: I'm not avoiding Jim. I'm going to sit at a mini golf course in a sweater, facing a windmill.

beats.text: Pam, he's bringing Shannon. She has a gel pen collection.

scenes.recap: Stanley vents to Creed about the outing, and Creed says something unsettling that nobody follows up.

beats.text: A pavilion. A windmill. Jim's girlfriend. I'm at 188 and I am not going to a windmill.
I once buried a tuba in Tunisia. I think about it on Thursdays.
Did I stutter?

scenes.venue: PALM HARBOR MINI GOLF AND GRIL
scenes.recap: At the entrance, Jim walks in with Shannon and Karen, and Pam ducks behind the scorecard stand.

beats.text: Welcome to Palm Harbor Mini Golf and Grille, home of the windmill!
Hey, Michael.
Jim! Pam is right behind the scorecards. I'm not lying for her anymore.
I'm reading the rules.
Is that her? The one with the card?
Karen.
What? The card is in the building.
Who's the lady behind the scorecards, Jim?
Halpert. You're here. Good.

beats.caption: Pam takes a rule sheet and walks toward the first hole.

scenes.venue: PALM HARBOR MINI GOLF AND GRIL
scenes.recap: Michael hands out bowling-pin trophies, skips Toby, then sits down and asks Toby how he is.

beats.text: Everybody gets a trophy! Michael Scott Mini Golf Invitational. It's a bowling pin, spray-painted gold.
That's a bowling pin, Michael.
It's a championship bowling pin.

beats.caption: sits alone at a picnic table, holding a plain scorecard

lines: Michael skipped me for the trophy. I'm used to it.
Then he came over and asked how I am. I don't know what to do with that.

beats.text: Toby, how are you doing? Actually. How are you?
You've never asked me that.
I'm trying to be present. It's exhausting.
The bumper boats aren't in fire code. But I'm okay.
Okay. Then I'll sit here. Be present. Good.

scenes.venue: PALM HARBOR MINI GOLF AND GRIL
scenes.recap: Jim finds Pam crouched behind the windmill hole, and she says she read his card three times and needs to talk, but not here.

beats.caption: crouches behind the giant windmill on hole six

beats.text: You're behind a windmill.
It's a good windmill.
I got your card. I read it. Three times, actually.
Three. Okay. And?

lines: She read it three times. That's more words than she's said to me since March.
Shannon is also being very supportive. Which is the worst part.

beats.text: Is Shannon nice?
She's really nice.
Good. I have something to tell you. It's not a windmill conversation.
Jim! Karen wants the scorecard. She says you're cheating on hole four.
Monday. Not here.

scenes.venue: PALM HARBOR MINI GOLF AND GRIL
scenes.recap: Dwight and Andy run through Monday's presentation at hole nine, agreeing on a grudging split of the call.

beats.text: Question: have you prepared a Monday agenda?
I prepared a presentation, a banjo, and a deep breath.
Mine has eleven bullet points. Yours has one, which says Dwight.
That's not even a real bullet point.
You do the talking. I do the eye contact. David Wallace respects eye contact.

beats.caption: offers a high five; Dwight stares at it until it lowers

beats.text: Why you two not fight? Fight is more fun.
Partners, Kevin. We're partners.

scenes.venue: PALM HARBOR MINI GOLF AND GRIL
scenes.recap: At the pavilion toast, Michael tries to be sincere, Roy warns Jim off, and Kelly calls Michael's kindness disgusting.

beats.text: Stamford and Scranton, one family. I'm glad everyone is here.
Stamford is the good branch.
Pam, June fourteenth. I got the caterer. Halpert, you called?
I called, Roy.
Don't make her sad, Halpert.

lines: Jan said my kindness is disgusting. Kelly said it too, just now. I'm not sure it's a compliment.
But I'll take it. Honestly, I'll take anything today.

beats.text: Michael, that was disgusting. Thank you.
That's what she said.

scenes.recap: In the parking lot, Jim asks Pam about Monday, Stanley is at 187, and the joke dies one more time.

beats.text: Monday?
Maybe. Ask me Monday.
Stanley, 187 days. That's what she said.

beats.caption: Stanley gets into his car without a word.

beats.text: Nobody say nothing.
